items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ralph Cooper, who was a dancer turned orchestra leader, was playing at the Lafayette one week and he had a very good show band. Ralph really knew show business. I saw the band during the early part of the week and really enjoyed its presentation.

ctx.x: When Arthur finished his set, they came off and I left my place to go and find the trumpet player. I told him my name, and that I was a trumpet player and it was my first night to New York. Also, that I liked his playing very much. He told me that his name was Leonard Davis. Later I got to know the other musicians who were Edgar Sampson, alto sax, Happy Cauldwell, a little fellow with a big voice and big tone on tenor sax; George Washington, trombone, Paul Barnet, banjo, and Billy Taylor, the tuba man
The drummer was Ralph..... I don't remember his last name, nor the name of the other alto.
I did not bother to listen to Fess Williams anymore but every time Arthur Gibbs played a set of 4 numbers, I found a place across from them where I could hear everything they did.
